before.test: TopicSponsor deleted request is denied in the same Service and after restart without recreation

after.creationAuthority: Existing deterministic topic and first-message IDs; existing native config request proof and deletion tombstone. A verified denial or unchanged replay returns the current config without publishing it again.
after.deliveryAuthority: The existing native admission v3 journal atomically writes an accepted entry with its scoped fingerprint, entry and message IDs. Fresh resolver checks precede admission/replay; History edits/deletions do not remove the acceptance proof.
cases: A real concurrent deletion after Flowlock initial History publication rejects the late ACK and a fresh-process replay; no directory is recreated.
Deletion during durable reservation prevents the renderer advance call and the queued success from returning as an available target.

Process is killed with SIGKILL after one renderer handoff. Cold restart retains uncertain status and original IDs, rejects a conflicting payload, never dispatches a second handoff and rejects a late terminal after deletion.

Legal duplicates return the original IDs; a different message, sender, ambiguous owner, or subsequent change of owner cannot reuse the receipt. After a normal drain and a cold start the original message can be edited or removed without a duplicate delivery.
Guarded deletion rejection leaves the primary config inode and content unchanged. Direct writes to a legitimate sibling still succeed with an active HistoryAuthority.
after.legacy: Recoverable v1/v2 entries retain their original IDs and uncertain status. A matching pending reply can acquire the v3 receipt; old v3 receipts and extension fields are preserved on subsequent journal writes. Settled pre-v3 replies without any request-to-message binding cannot be attributed retrospectively. No historical data is migrated; deletion blocks replay even when old acceptance proof is absent.
after.notInScope: TopicSponsor mode=new_topic independent task dispatch remains outside this fix.

electron.host: isolated real Electron, registered native desktop distributed TopicSponsor, loopback WebSocket peer
